JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 30-11-2024 at about 12-15 a.m. the petitioner was traveling in Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA-01-AN-0568 along with his friends from Tumkur - Magadi road and when the Tempo Traveler vehicle reached near Bylanjaneya Temple, Garudappa circle, Andrahalli main road, at that time the driver of Tempo Traveler by driving in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the road side tree, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately petitioner was shifted to Prakriya Hospital, Tumkur road,
wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Boss Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient for a period of 7 days.
So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.7,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was working as Agriculturist cum delivery boy and earning monthly Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, he is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability & loss of income.
4. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA-01-AN- 0568 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex- parte.

5. The respondent no.2/ the Insurer of Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA-01-AN-0568 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to Bharath S vs Jai Maruthi Travels on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192889616/
2 the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

sentences.text: The respondent no.2 has disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

The respondent no.2 further contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding a valid driving license and the said vehicle was not having permit and FC and that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 30-11-2024 at about 12- 15 am., near Bylanjaneya Temple,
Garudappa circle, Andrahalli mian road, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Temple Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-0568?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and examined two witnesses as P.W.2 and P.W3 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P21.
During the cross-examination of RW.1, the learned counsel for petitioner has confronted the documents and got them marked as Ex.P27 and Ex.P28.

On the other hand,
Somashekara N -PSI, Kamakshipalya Traffic PS is examined as RW.1.

The respondent no. 2 has examined its Legal Executive as RW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA-01-AN-0568, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 30-11-2024 at about 12-15 a.m. when the petitioner was traveling in Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA-01-AN-0568 (herein after called as the offending vehicle) along with his friends from Tumkur - Magadi road and when the Tempo Traveler vehicle reached near Bylanjaneya Temple, Garudappa circle, Andrahalli main road, at that time the driver of Tempo Traveler by driving in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the Bharath S vs Jai Maruthi Travels on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192889616/
3 road side tree, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, statement of eye witnesses, spot mahazar, sketch, notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act, reply given thereon, IMV report, wound certificate,
charge sheet etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Bharath S (ie) petitioner, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.0719/2024 of Kamakshipalya Traffic Police Station, for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(a) of BNS 2023.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of BNS 2023 and U/Sec. 134(a & b), 187 of MV Act.
13.

The respondent no.2 in their written statement have disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident but during the cross examination of PW.1 and RW.1 who is the investigating officer no signal suggestion has been posed by denying the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

If the medical records are perused, soon after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Prakriya Hospital and from there he was shifted to Boss Hospital wherein the history of accident is mentioned as "RTA".
It is not in dispute that at the time of accident petitioner was traveling in Tempo Travels bearing No.KA-01-AN-0568.
IN the accident no other vehicle was involved.
The offending vehicle hit to the standing tree result of which severe damage was caused to the vehicle which is evident from the IMV report.
Hence, there is no reason to believe that offending vehicle was falsely implicated in the case.

14. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has bent upon contended that at the time of accident the driver and all the inmates of the offending vehicle were under the influence of alcohol and the driver of the offending vehicle by name Darshan Rathod under the influence of alcohol had driven the vehicle.
Hence, there is violation of policy condition, hence the respondent no.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
The learned counsel has mainly relied upon the statement of the petitioner as per Ex.P1 given before the Station House Officer of the jurisdictional PS to substantiate their argument/defence.
15. If Ex.P1 is perused, the petitioner had given statement as per Ex.P1 on 02-12-2024.
The accident in question has occurred on 29-11-2024.
Hence, there is delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint.

But as observed supra, from the medical records it can be gathered that soon after the accident petitioner had taken treatment at first at Prakriya Hospital and thereafter at Boss Hospital wherein MLC was registered and police intimation was sent to the jurisdictional Police on 01-12-2024.
The police officials could have visited the hospital on the very date of the receipt of the police intimation and could have recorded the statement of the victim.

Further as per the evidence of RW.1 - The Investigating Officer, on the date of accident itself they had the knowledge of the accident and the ASI of their police station had visited the spot soon after the accident and he had also visited the scene of occurrence in the morning hours on 30-11-2024.
But they have not thought it necessary to register FIR.

It is deposed by RW.1 that since police intimation was received on 01- 12-2024, they Bharath S vs Jai Maruthi Travels on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192889616/
4 have registered the FIR on receiving the statement of injured.

sentences.text: Anyhow the petitioner has proved that offending vehicle was involved in the accident and he had sustained injuries as the impact of the accident.
Hence, delay in lodging the complaint do not go to the root of the case of petitioner.

16. If the averments of Ex.P1 ie., statement of the injured is read in whole, wherein he has stated that the driver of the offending vehicle ie., Darshan Rathod had asked them to have liquor in the vehicle and driver had already purchased liquor and kept the liquor bottle in the offending vehicle,and the petitioner and Srikanth had also purchased Beer from MRP shop and they have consumed alcohol in the TT and having consumed alcohol they went for rounds in the TT.

17. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 by referring the aforesaid statement of the petitioner has vehemently submitted that the petitioner himself at an undisputed point of time had admitted the consumption of alcohol by all the inmates of the offending vehicle including the driver and the very admission of petitioner would sufficient to hold that on the date of accident even driver was also under the influence of alcohol.

Hence, according to the learned counsel, the court can safely arrive at the conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle under the influence of alcohol had driven the vehicle and thereby violated the policy condition.

The learned counsel in further has argued that though in the statement of petitioner he has clearly stated about the consumption of alcohol by all but the investigating Officer for the reason best known to him has not registered the FIR by invoking Sec. 185 of IMV Act for drink and driving and though blood stain was in the vehicle,
the investigating officer thought it not necessary to collect the blood sample and send it for Scientific Investigation and no steps has been taken to subject the inmates and driver to breath analysis test and thereby the Investigating Officer has not properly investigated the case and just to help the petitioner and driver, he has filed charge sheet without inserting section 185 of the MV Act.
18.

Per contra, the learned counsel for petitioner has referred the statement given by the inmates of the offending vehicle under Sec.162 of Cr.PC and the confessional statement of the accused wherein they have stated that since driver had to drive the vehicle he did not consume alcohol and rest of the inmates had consumed alcohol.

The learned counsel in further has referred the medical evidence and the charge sheet wherein there is no mention about consumption of alcohol by the driver and submitted that if really driver was under the influence of alcohol he would have been charge sheeted even for drunk and drive.

19. In the light of the contention taken by the respective parties, if the materials placed on record is perused, as observed supra, it is true that the complainant/ petitioner in his statement has stated about the consumption of alcohol but he has not stated in specific terms that even driver Darshan Rathod had also consumed alcohol.
So far as the collection of blood samples lying in the offending vehicle is concerned, there are altogether five persons were traveling in the said vehicle.
The driver was in the driving seat.
If the photographs are perused, blood stains were lying behind the driver seat.

Hence, even if blood sample was collected and it was sent for Scientific Investigation it would not have given accurate report whether the said blood sample is of the driver and whether the blood sample contains alcohol contents allegedly consumed by Darshan Rathod ie., driver.
Further the counsel for petitioner has relied upon statement given by the inmates of the vehicle under Sec. 162 of Cr.PC.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 while marking the statement of witnesses under Bharath S vs Jai Maruthi Travels on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192889616/
5 Sec. 162 Cr.PC through RW.1 has raised objection stating that the statement u/Sec. 162 of Cr.PC cannot be relied upon.

sentences.text:
20. This court is of the opinion that the statement taken by police during investigation have limited,
yet specific relevancy in MVC cases.
Statement
recorded
u/Sec.162 is not evidence on its own but it cannot be used to prove the truth of its contains.

The primary purpose is to contradict a witness ie.,
different from what they told the police, the opposite party can use the 162 statement to prove contradiction.
21.

If the statement given by the witnesses u/Sec. 162 Cr.PC is looked into for limited purpose, on 03-12- 2024 ie., on the very next date of the statement given by the petitioner as per Ex.P1, the rest of the eye witnesses had given their statement stating that on the said date driver did not consume consumed alcohol because he had to drive the vehicle.
22. As per the statement of witnesses the driver had taken treatment at MR Hospital and petitioner at first had taken treatment at Prakriya Hospital and then he was shifted to Boss Hospital.

When driver had taken treatment at MR Hospital, if really driver had consumed alcohol, the respondent no.2 could have taken steps to summon the medical records from MR Hospital to prove before the court that the driver was also under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident.

Even if it is taken for a while for the sake of argument by relying upon the Ex.P1 that the driver had also consumed alcohol but there is no evidence before the court the quantum of alcohol consumed by the driver.
If driver had consumed alcohol of the quantity of 30 mg / 100 ml it is permissible and no offence would attract u/Sec. 185 of the MV Act.
It is illegal if blood alcohol exceeds 30 mg per 100 ml.
Hence, the materials placed on record would not sufficient to hold that the driver of the offending vehicle had driven the vehicle under the influence of alcohol .
23. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, it is not in dispute that at the time of accident petitioner was traveling in the offending vehicle.
There is no other vehicle involved in the accident.
The offending vehicle hit to the standing tree result of which the branches of the tree also fell down.
Hence from which it can be gathered the speed at which the offending vehicle was at the time of accident.
Further the offending vehicle was also severely damaged.
Hence, from the aforesaid facts it can be said that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are at Ex.P7 and Ex.P9.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Boss Multispeciality Hospital on 01-12-2024 to 06-12-204 for a period of 5 days.
As per the wound certificate, petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature.

25. Mahesh Kumar - Medical Record Technician at BOSS Multispeciality Hospital is examined as PW.2 and through him Police Intimation, MLC, Case sheet, X- ray film are got marked as Ex.P.16 to Ex.P19.

sentences.text: Dr. S A Somashekara - Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore is examined as Pw.3 and through him OPD and x-ray are marked as Ex.P20 and Ex.P21.
PW.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 15-10-2025 clinically, radiologically for assessment of disability.

PW.3 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent disability of both lower limbs at 60% and on whole body disability at 30% and that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants of both sides which would cost around Rs.50,000/- in private set up.
27. If the evidence of PW.3 is perused, he is not a treated doctor.

As per the evidence of PW.3 out of the two fractures one is united and petitioner require further treatment at the cost of Rs.50,000/-
and that he has assessed only the physical disability but not the functional disability.
The PW.3 having assessed the disability on particular limb at 60%, assessed the disability on whole body at 30%.
In a judgment reported in SLP (Civil) 2738/2019 c/w 2739/2019, the disability on whole body would be the 1/4th of the particular limb.
28. If the calculation made in the aforesaid ruling is considered, then the PW.3 ought to have assessed the disability on whole body at 15%.
Hence considering the evidence of PW.3 this court is of the opinion that PW3 has assessed the disability on higher side.

Hence, this court inclines to consider the disability at 15% instead of 30%.
29.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
30. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
31. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bill for Rs.2,28,836-, as per Ex.P13.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.2,28,836/-.
32.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 26 years and he was working as a Agriculturist cum delivery boy and was earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and the place of residence, assess the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
33.
The petitioner has sustained two grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 5 days as an inpatient in Boss Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 4 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for 4 months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.66,000/-
(16,500X4) towards loss of income during the laid down period .

7 34.

sentences.text: From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Boss Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore.
Further for 5 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking into consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
35. The petitioner has contended that, he was aged about 26 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P11/Aadhar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 09-07-1998 that means he was aged about 26 years.
Hence considering the copy of Aadhaar card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 26 years at the time of accident.

36. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and if 15% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 26 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 is '17'.
So by applying the multiplier '17' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.5,04,900/- (i.e., 16,500 x 15% x 17x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,04,900/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
37. PW.3 has stated that petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implant at both sites, the estimate of said surgery is around Rs.50,000/- in private set up.
The PW.3 has not stated the estimated cost of future surgery and has not given estimation.

Hence, this court inclines to award future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.
38.
The petitioner at his age of 26 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards loss of comfort and amenities, thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 75,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs. 2,28,836/-
 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 66,000/-
 laid up period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant

Rs . 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food

5. Future Loss of Income Rs. 5,04,900/-
 6. Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
 7. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs. 50,000/-

Total Rs. Rs.9,79,736/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,79,736/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Seventy Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Thirty Six only).

sentences.text: As regarding liability is concerned, respondent no.1 is the RC owner and respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
40. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.9,79,736/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA No.I.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.9,80,236/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Eighty Thousand Two Hundred Thirty Six only).

After deducting cost of Rs 500/- and future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/- balance sum of Rs.9,49,736/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 6th day of March 2026.)

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 30-11-2024 at about 12- 15 am., near Bylanjaneya Temple,
Garudappa circle, Andrahalli mian road, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Temple Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AN-0568?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b) of BNS 2023 and U/Sec. 134(a & b), 187 of MV Act.
13.
Hence, there is no reason to believe that offending vehicle was falsely implicated in the case.
15. If Ex.P1 is perused, the petitioner had given statement as per Ex.P1 on 02-12-2024.
Hence, there is delay of 3 days in lodging the complaint.
The police officials could have visited the hospital on the very date of the receipt of the police intimation and could have recorded the statement of the victim.
20. This court is of the opinion that the statement taken by police during investigation have limited,
yet specific relevancy in MVC cases.
u/Sec.162 is not evidence on its own but it cannot be used to prove the truth of its contains.
The primary purpose is to contradict a witness ie.,
different from what they told the police, the opposite party can use the 162 statement to prove contradiction.
21.
If the statement given by the witnesses u/Sec. 162 Cr.PC is looked into for limited purpose, on 03-12- 2024 ie., on the very next date of the statement given by the petitioner as per Ex.P1, the rest of the eye witnesses had given their statement stating that on the said date driver did not consume consumed alcohol because he had to drive the vehicle.
When driver had taken treatment at MR Hospital, if really driver had consumed alcohol, the respondent no.2 could have taken steps to summon the medical records from MR Hospital to prove before the court that the driver was also under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident.
Even if it is taken for a while for the sake of argument by relying upon the Ex.P1 that the driver had also consumed alcohol but there is no evidence before the court the quantum of alcohol consumed by the driver.
If driver had consumed alcohol of the quantity of 30 mg / 100 ml it is permissible and no offence would attract u/Sec. 185 of the MV Act.
It is illegal if blood alcohol exceeds 30 mg per 100 ml.
Hence, the materials placed on record would not sufficient to hold that the driver of the offending vehicle had driven the vehicle under the influence of alcohol .
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and the place of residence, assess the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
33.
The petitioner has sustained two grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 5 days as an inpatient in Boss Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 4 months as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during the laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for 4 months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.66,000/-
(16,500X4) towards loss of income during the laid down period .

Total Rs. Rs.9,79,736/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.9,79,736/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Seventy Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Thirty Six only).

40. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.9,79,736/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA No.I.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.9,80,236/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Eighty Thousand Two Hundred Thirty Six only).
After deducting cost of Rs 500/- and future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/- balance sum of Rs.9,49,736/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
